decisive_items: hypodense mass containing areas of calcification
mass appeared to nearly obliterate the lumens of the main and hilar pulmonary arteries
dilation of the main pulmonary artery
response.rationale: The imaging findings of a calcified hypodense mass filling and nearly obliterating the main and hilar pulmonary arteries, without valve involvement or peripheral extension, are classic for pulmonary artery sarcoma. This distinguishes it from chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (which typically lacks a discrete calcified mass), pulmonary embolism (acute, no calcification), and other listed entities. The elevated D-dimer is nonspecific and does not contradict the diagnosis.

rejected.why: Tricuspid regurgitation is a valvular condition; the mass and vascular occlusion are not explained.
Fibrosing mediastinitis typically causes extrinsic compression, not an intraluminal calcified mass.
Pulmonary artery aneurysm is dilation without an obstructive calcified mass.
Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma usually presents with diffuse perfusion defects, not a discrete calcified mass.
Pulmonary embolism is acute and does not show calcification within a mass.
Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension may cause occlusion but lacks a calcified intraluminal mass.
